lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Richard, this is Luis. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Did you hit your goal this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I didn't do it. I'm just so tired, I don't have it in me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is anyone else at home able to cook?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to stop eating out so much.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've always eaten late, that's how we do it at home.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not really trying.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, yes. Everything at the store costs so much.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I got home late every day this week. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to stop eating out so much.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I'm doing the best I can.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to cook at home 4 nights next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If work gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Fatigue as reason not to change
Cultural habit as reason to stay
Checks if participant can do it
Asks for backup plan for barriers
Sets midweek text and follow-up call
Requests later time due to appointment

flags.reason: Repeated directive advice ('You have to stop eating out') without asking permission.
Imposes priority; pushes rather than exploring the participant's own values.
'You're not really trying' is confrontational and undermines rapport.
Health warning used as pressure; may increase defensiveness.
Repeats the same directive right after emphasizing autonomy, contradicting it.
Sets a 4-night cooking target unilaterally; participant responds 'I don't know'.
Participant sees possible household help; coach did not reinforce or explore it.
Concrete step (fridge reminder) not acknowledged or elaborated.
'Yeah, I think so' is tentative change talk; coach moved straight to a plan.
Participant asked for a later time due to appointment; coach ignored it and closed.

score.summary: The coach relied heavily on directives and warnings ('You have to,' 'You're not really trying,' 'Let's put you down') that pushed the participant toward defensiveness and 'I don't know' responses. Real change talk (fridge reminder, daughter's help, backup lunch plan) went largely unreinforced, and the participant's scheduling request was ignored.
strengths: Line 10: complex reflection reframing the missed goal as 'still figuring out what works' was a good non-judgmental move.
Line 31: emphasize autonomy ('It's your plan') was the right instinct, though it was undercut by line 32.
Line 38: open question about a backup plan for barriers helped the participant generate their own solution at line 39.
Line 40: set a concrete midweek check-in and follow-up call.
coaching_tips: Replace lines 14, 16, and 32 with a question such as 'What makes it hard to cook at home on busy nights?' to elicit the participant's own reasons.
Reflect and reinforce the change talk at lines 19 and 28 (e.g., 'You already put a reminder on the fridge, and your daughter is helping') before moving on.
Drop 'You're not really trying' at line 18; use a reflection that acknowledges effort, such as 'You're doing the best you can with a lot on your plate.'
At line 36, ask permission or offer options rather than assigning 4 nights: 'Would it help to aim for a number of nights that feels doable?'
Honor the scheduling request at line 41 by offering a later time before closing; summarize the plan at the end of the call.
